To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is an increasing tendency of CM utilization in Taiwan.
the utilization of CM increased from the first year (1997) to the last year (2003) of our study period and that CM and WM are used in similar patterns in the Taiwanese population.
the utilization of CM and the frequency of CM services were higher in female, elderly, and residents in central and southern areas of Taiwan.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the utilization patterns of WM and CM in the national insurance system.
the utilization of CM and Western medicine in Taiwan.
the utilization patterns of WM and CM, the demographic characteristics, and primary indications influencing their choice of medical services in Taiwan.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CM and WM are complementary in Taiwan, but CM is more frequently used for chronic diseases.
the use of CM in Taiwan is increasing and that CM is mainly used in the treatment of respiratory diseases.
the use of CM and WM has been increasing in Taiwan, and that there is a need for further research on the appropriate use of CM and the effectiveness of WM in the future.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the utilization of CM and the utilization of WM were influenced by different factors.
there is an increasing use of CM in recent years, but the use of WM is still higher than that of CM.
CM is used more frequently by females, the elderly and those living in rural areas and that CM is used mainly for the treatment of diseases of the respiratory system and gastrointestinal system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CM has become an important component in the dual medical system in Taiwan and should be considered in the health-care policies for the elderly and the disadvantaged population.
CM has a complementary role with WM in Taiwan.
the utilization patterns of the two medical systems are different.
